payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_fold.py::test_a_task_whose_record_holds_run_created_folds_onto_a_run_of_its_own stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The fold puts a task back on the row it held even while another task names it, so a bare task reads the status a run fact gave its neighbour.' applied to saffron/ledger.py as an edit. The claim was 'A task whose record holds either run fact folds onto a `runs` row of its own, finished or not, and a task with neither never joins it. That covers a task holding `run_finished` with no `run_created`, after an older task with neither. Folding the same record again into the same ledger leaves one row per task. A record that holds neither run fact folds as at base. Its tasks at one `base_sha` share one row, `RUNNING` with a null `ended_at`, through a second fold as well. In a record where one task holds the run facts and another does not, the one that does not reads `RUNNING` with a null `ended_at`. That holds whether it is the older task or the younger, through a second fold as well. A record may grow a `run_finished` between two folds. With an older task holding run facts beside a younger bare one, the row count stays two across both folds. With two bare tasks sharing a row, it goes from one to two, the older or the younger gaining the fact. Only the task that gains it reads `COMPLETE`. Folded back into the ledger that wrote it, a task keeps the row it ran on, twice over. Its `task_run` is that row, the ledger holds one row, and the row keeps its `batch_id`, its `preflight` and its baseline gate result.', and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
